blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India.

items: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) was termed the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) were added based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12 to 35) and are legally enforceable in courts.
Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Part IV and serve as guidelines for governance.
